Nothing in the configuration signals the difference, and the omission is not the outcome of a decision recorded anywhere — the interceptors simply post-date the forks. {{config-browser}}'s {{configBrowserDefault}} delegates to {{validationWorkflowStack}}, which derives from {{defaultStack}}, so it is unaffected. h3. Proposed change Add {{coep}}, {{coop}} and {{fetchMetadata}} to {{restDefaultStack}} and {{beanValidationDefaultStack}}, with the same parameters {{defaultStack}} uses, positioned as they are in {{defaultStack}}. h3. Notes * Affects 6.x and 7.x alike: {{WW-5083}} shipped in 6.0.0, and both plugin stacks lack the interceptors on {{main}} and on {{support/struts-6-x-x}}. * This is a behaviour change for existing REST and Bean Validation deployments: {{fetchMetadata}} rejects requests whose {{Sec-Fetch-Site}} marks them cross-site, so a REST API deliberately serving cross-origin browser clients will start seeing 403s unless it configures {{exemptedPaths}} or disables the interceptor. It should be called out in the migration notes. * The wider point is structural: a plugin that replaces {{defaultStack}} inherits nothing from it afterwards, so every future addition to {{defaultStack}} has to be mirrored by hand into each fork. Worth considering whether these stacks can extend the core stack rather than restate it.

title: REST XML handlers throw NullPointerException when there is no target to render
Description: {{JacksonXmlHandler.fromObject}} and {{JuneauXmlHandler.fromObject}} dereference the object they are asked to render before checking it: {code:java}public String fromObject(ActionInvocation invocation, Object obj, String resultCode, Writer stream) throws IOException { LOG.debug("Converting an object of {} into string", obj.getClass().getName()); ... } {code} {{RestActionInvocation.selectTarget()}} sets the target to {{null}} for a POST, PUT or DELETE that produced no errors while {{restrictToGet}} is enabled (the default), and since WW-5718 also for a request an interceptor short-circuited with a bare HTTP status ({{fetchMetadata}} returning {{403}}). {{DefaultContentTypeHandlerManager.handleResult}} then calls {{fromObject}} with that {{null}} target. For the JSON handler this is harmless (Jackson writes {{null}}). For the two XML handlers it throws a {{NullPointerException}}, which {{RestActionInvocation.invoke()}} catches: it sets the response status to 500, puts the exception on the value stack and re-runs {{processResult()}}, so the client receives a serialised {{NullPointerException}} (including its stack trace) as the XML body of what was a successful write - or, for the status case, as the body of the 403. {{XStreamHandler.fromObject}} already guards this with {{if (obj != null)}}. The two Jackson/Juneau XML handlers should do the same and write nothing (or an empty document) for a {{null}} target. Reproduction: a {{rest-default}} action answering a POST with the {{xml}} extension under the default {{restrictToGet=true}}; the response is a 500 with an XML-serialised {{NullPointerException}} instead of the intended status with an empty body. Found while reviewing WW-5718; not caused by it.

title: ActionNameSpecificityComparator can rank a broad ** pattern ahead of a narrower */* one
Description: Follow-up to WW-3784 (7.3.0), which introduced {{ActionNameSpecificityComparator}} in the Convention plugin so annotated wildcard actions are matched most-specific-first instead of in class-scan order. The comparator's keys, in order, are: fewer wildcard tokens first, more literal characters first, fewer path-spanning {{\*\*}} tokens first, then lexical. Because the raw token count comes before the {{\*\*}} count, a pattern with one {{\*\*}} outranks a pattern with two {{\*}} even though {{\*\*}} crosses {{/}} and {{\*}} does not ({{WildcardHelper}} MATCH\_PATH vs MATCH\_FILE) — so {{\*\*}} is the broader pattern of the two and should lose: * {{a/\*\*}} — 1 wildcard token, 1 path-spanning * {{a/\*/\*}} — 2 wildcard tokens, 0 path-spanning Today the first sorts ahead of the second and shadows it for {{a/x/y}}. Proposed refinement: lift the {{**}}-count key above the raw token-count key (fewer {{\*\*}} first, then fewer tokens, then more literals). Ordering stays per-package by design. Worth a test pair in {{ActionNameSpecificityComparatorTest}} for exactly the {{a/\*\*}} vs {{a/\*/\*}} case, plus the {{\{var\}}} equivalent for {{NamedVariablePatternMatcher}} users. Fix version intentionally left unset.

title: null can no longer be passed as parameter to interceptor
Description: Upgrading from 7.2.1 to 7.3.0 seems to have made a change so that null cannot be passed as a parameter to the ActionFileUploadInterceptor. I have an interceptor like this: {code:java} <interceptor name="myFileUpload" class="org.apache.struts2.interceptor.ActionFileUploadInterceptor"> <param name="maximumSize">128000000</param> </interceptor>{code} That interceptor is then included in a global interceptor stack called myFileUploadStack. Later in some specific actions I want to set the maximumSize to null (no limit) and I do this: {code:java} <interceptor-ref name="myFileUploadStack"> <param name="myFileUpload.maximumSize">null</param> </interceptor-ref>{code} This used to work until 7.2.1, but in 7.3.0 it gives an error: The upload validation policy could not be resolved, rejecting the file: file "test.pdf"; unresolved parameters: maximumSize Looking at the code and the release notes of 7.3.0, I can find that this probably relates to the changes made in WithLazyParams.java and AbstractFileUploadInterceptor.java (using a policy) as part of WW-5659. But I do not see in the release notes anything about this being intended or what the migration path would be. The javadoc of WithLazyParams.resolveInto() mentions null and empty value becoming unresolved, but not what to do about it. Obviously, I can set a very large number or create a second interceptor and interceptorStack to get around this, but I felt that this should be reported so that either it can be fixed, or it can be confirmed as the intended behaviour and if so, perhaps write something about it in the release notes (under Breaking changes) or in a migration guide.

title: BeanValidationInterceptor resolves the interpolated constraint message as a text key instead of the message template
Description: {{BeanValidationInterceptor}} builds the field and action error text from {{ConstraintViolation.getMessage()}}, which is the message *after* the Bean Validation provider has interpolated it, and passes that string to the Struts text provider ({{getText(...)}}) as the text key. The key a developer declares is the constraint's {{message}} attribute, which is what {{ConstraintViolation.getMessageTemplate()}} returns. Using the interpolated message as the key means: * a developer-declared Struts key only resolves when the provider leaves the message untouched; * provider-interpolated text that matches no key is not shown as the provider produced it, but is handed to the text provider as default text and processed again, as if it were a Struts message. The plugin documentation only promises that the {{message}} value is looked up as a Struts key; it does not say that provider-produced text goes through the text provider. h2. Change Resolve the error text from the template, and keep the provider's message otherwise: * look up {{getMessageTemplate()}} in the Struts bundles, and call {{getText}} with it only when {{hasKey}} finds it; * otherwise use {{ConstraintViolation.getMessage()}} as-is, as literal text; * never pass the interpolated message to any text-provider method ({{getText}}, {{hasKey}}, {{findText}}). h2. Tests * A constraint whose provider-interpolated message contains text that the Struts text provider would otherwise process is reported exactly as the provider produced it. * Existing tests where {{message}} is a Struts key keep resolving through the bundle. Apply the same change on the 6.x line. h2. Documentation The Bean Validation plugin page should state that {{message}} is looked up as a Struts key, and that a message produced by the provider is shown literally.

title: Upgrade OGNL to version 3.4.15
Description: Upgrade OGNL from 3.4.14 to [3.4.15|https://github.com/orphan-oss/ognl/releases]. OGNL 3.4.15 includes orphan-oss/ognl#660 (3.4.x backport of #658): {{OgnlRuntime.hasSetProperty}} no longer reports a property as settable when its only backing member is a static or final field, which {{setFieldValue}} refuses to write. {{CompoundRootAccessor}} relies on that answer to decide which value stack object takes a parameter, so it now matches what OGNL can actually write. Builds on WW-5759, which moves Struts to OGNL 3.4.14.

title: Make struts.convention.result.path scopable per package
Description: A follow-up to the package-scoped constants from [WW-3476|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/WW-3476], whose first adopter was [WW-5768|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/WW-5768] ({{struts.ui.theme}}, {{struts.ui.templateDir}}). h2. Goal Allow a parent package to set the Convention result path for the actions placed under it: {code:xml}<package name="admin-base" extends="convention-default"> <scoped-constant name="struts.convention.result.path" value="/WEB-INF/admin/"/> </package> {code} Today the same effect needs {{@ResultPath}} on every action class or package. h2. Why it needs more than WW-5768 {{ScopedConstantProvider.getValue(name)}} resolves the package from the current {{ActionInvocation}}. The Convention plugin reads the result path in two places: # *At startup*, in {{DefaultResultMapBuilder.build(...)}} via {{ConventionsService.determineResultPath(Class)}}. There is no invocation, so {{getValue(name)}} always returns the global value. However, {{build()}} receives the action's {{PackageConfig}}. {{PackageBasedActionConfigBuilder}} passes {{pkgCfg.build()}}, which was created with {{addParent(parentPkg)}}, so {{getAllScopedConstants()}} already includes the parent's overrides. # *At runtime*, in {{ConventionUnknownHandler.determinePath(...)}} via {{determineResultPath(ActionConfig)}}, for action-less results. {{actionConfig}} may be {{null}} there. Both need a lookup by package rather than by invocation. One option is a {{getValue(String name, PackageConfig packageConfig)}} on {{ScopedConstantProvider}}, with {{getValue(name)}} delegating to it for the current invocation's package. h2. Proposed change * Register a {{ScopableConstants}} bean in the Convention plugin's {{struts-plugin.xml}} returning {{struts.convention.result.path}}. * Resolve the result path from the action's package in both places, keeping this precedence: ## {{@ResultPath}} on the action class or package ## the package's scoped constant (including inherited ones) ## the global {{struts.convention.result.path}} h2. Tests * A scoped override on the parent package changes the location of results built at startup. * {{@ResultPath}} still wins over the override. * An action-less result resolved by {{ConventionUnknownHandler}} uses the override. * With no override, the global path is used. h2. Docs On the struts-site, list the constant on the scoped-constants section of {{core-developers/package-configuration.md}}, and mention it on the Convention plugin page.

title: ExecuteAndWaitInterceptor re-stores the transaction token from request parameters instead of the token validated in the request
Description: {{ExecuteAndWaitInterceptor}} puts a transaction token back into the session every time it returns the wait result. It reads the {{token}} request parameter as the value and the {{struts.token.name}} request parameter as the name, and passes both to {{TokenHelper.setSessionToken(...)}}. This was added in WW-1741 so that an action using both {{token}} and {{execAndWait}} keeps accepting its wait-page refreshes after {{TokenInterceptor}} has consumed the token. The interceptor does not check that a token was validated in the current request, though, so it stores whatever name and value any request supplies, including requests to an execAndWait action that has no token check at all, such as one using the shipped {{executeAndWaitStack}}. The session token store is otherwise written only with server-generated values: the token tag calls {{TokenHelper.setToken}}, which generates a random GUID. A later {{TokenHelper.validToken()}} accepts whatever value is in the store, so a value taken from request parameters is treated the same as one the server generated. The value and the name are also read inconsistently: the value always comes from the default {{token}} parameter, while the name comes from {{struts.token.name}}. h2. Change * {{TokenHelper.validToken()}} records the token name and value it accepted in the current {{ActionContext}}. * {{ExecuteAndWaitInterceptor}} re-stores only that recorded pair, and stores nothing when no token was validated in the current request. * {{ExecuteAndWaitInterceptor}} no longer reads the token from request parameters. h2. Tests * An execAndWait action without a token interceptor returns the wait result and leaves the session token store unchanged, for any token name supplied in the request. * An action using {{token}} and {{execAndWait}} keeps accepting the wait-page refresh that carries the validated token. * The same holds with {{tokenSession}} in place of {{token}}. Apply the same change on the 6.x line.

title: default values are restored for some properties on ModelDriven bean
Description: Some curl tests on the same ModelDriven action (in a package that extends both rest-default and json-default) have changed their result regarding the Struts version and it is summary by: ||Client query||Struts 7.1.1||upper|| |JSON|done|done| |form-data|done|failed| Since WW-5626 (or perhaps some related changes), the model bean of a ModelDriven action does not retain the values set by ParameterInterceptor unless it is null by default in a fresh instance otherwise the default value (in its constructor) overrides the client value. Looking at: https://struts.apache.org/core-developers/struts-parameter-annotation One solution we found is to set: {{struts.parameters.requireAnnotations=false}} But on model bean it should not be necessary to annotate if we understand well the documentation.

title: REST two-phase body copy writes constructor defaults over values already set on the target
Description: Follow-up to [WW-5789|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/WW-5789], which covered the handlers that do not read the body at all. When {{struts.parameters.requireAnnotations=true}} and the selected content-type handler does not implement {{AuthorizationAwareContentTypeHandler}}, {{ContentTypeInterceptor.applyTwoPhaseDeserialize}} creates a fresh instance of the target with its no-arg constructor, lets the handler fill it from the body, and then copies every non-null property from that instance onto the real target. The copy cannot tell a value the body supplied from a value the constructor assigned, so a property the body omits is still copied when it has a non-null constructor default. That overwrites whatever was on the target before the {{rest}} interceptor ran: a value bound by {{params}}, or one loaded in {{prepare()}}. The same happens in three shapes: a scalar with a constructor default, a collection initialised in the constructor (an empty list replaces a populated one on the target), and a nested bean initialised in the constructor (the copy recurses into it and resets the target's nested leaves). Affected handlers: {{XStreamHandler}} (shipped, registered by the application) and any application-provided handler that does not declare the marker. The handlers shipped as default ({{JacksonJsonHandler}}, {{JacksonXmlHandler}}, {{JuneauXmlHandler}}) are not affected, they authorize during deserialization. The JSON plugin uses a different mechanism and is not affected. Example: a ModelDriven model declares {{private String status = "new";}}. The request carries {{status=approved}} as a query parameter and an XML body that only contains {{name}}. After the stack runs, {{status}} is {{new}}. h2. Design Fix the copy, not the handlers. The affected handlers are opt-in or external and cannot report which properties they set, so the interceptor has to work it out on its own. * Build a second, untouched fresh instance of the target as a baseline next to the one the handler fills. * Copy a property only when its filled value differs from the baseline value, compared with {{Objects.deepEquals}} so arrays compare by content. A nested bean the handler instantiated compares by identity and therefore counts as changed, which is what is wanted. * Thread the baseline through the nested-bean recursion. When the baseline's nested value is null but the filled one is not, use a fresh instance of the nested class as the baseline at that level. When that class has no no-arg constructor, fall back to today's behaviour for that subtree. * Collections, maps and arrays are compared against the baseline at the property level only. Their elements are already rebuilt as new objects, so skipping defaults inside them would change nothing. * No public API change: {{ContentTypeHandler}}, {{AuthorizationAwareContentTypeHandler}} and the public surface of {{ContentTypeInterceptor}} stay as they are. No new configuration constant: a switch whose old setting is the defect has no sensible default. * The existing null-skip rule stays. Document the new default-skip rule next to it, in one place. Known limits, to be stated in the docs: * A body value equal to the constructor default, sent while the target holds a different value, is no longer applied. This mirrors the null ambiguity accepted in WW-5624. * Non-deterministic defaults such as {{UUID.randomUUID()}} or {{Instant.now()}} always differ from the baseline and keep being copied, as today. * The target's constructor runs twice per request on this path. Rejected: deserializing into a deep copy of the target. It would remove the ambiguity entirely, but needs a reflective deep copy of arbitrary object graphs, and a shallow copy would let the handler mutate the target's nested objects before authorization. Behaviour changes only when all three hold: {{requireAnnotations=true}}, a non-aware handler, and a property with a non-null constructor default. Applications on the default handlers see nothing. Tests to add in {{ContentTypeInterceptorIntegrationTest}}, with a non-aware handler that sets some properties and leaves others: omitted scalar default kept; set scalar applied; omitted collection default kept; omitted nested default kept; partially set nested bean applies only the set leaf; the documented limit pinned by name. Docs: a paragraph under the 7.2.0 enforcement note on the REST plugin page, and a line in the Version Notes. Out of scope, candidates for their own tickets: making {{XStreamHandler}} authorization-aware so no shipped handler is left on the two-phase path, and deprecating the two-phase path for removal at 8.0.0 once that is done.

title: Verify HTTP method restrictions for Convention plugin actions
Description: Follow-up to WW-3717, which adds an {{http-method}} attribute to {{<action>}} in {{struts.xml}}, enforced by {{HttpMethodInterceptor}}, with a 405 response (and an {{Allow}} header) when no {{bad-request}} result is mapped. Actions discovered by the Convention plugin have no XML declaration, so they cannot use the new attribute. The expectation is that they are already covered by the existing annotations ({{@HttpGet}}, {{@HttpPost}}, {{@HttpPut}}, {{@HttpDelete}}, {{@HttpGetOrPost}}, {{@AllowedHttpMethod}}) on the action class or method. Verify this and pick one outcome: * *Covered:* add tests in the Convention plugin that pin it: an annotated Convention action (class-level and method-level, including an {{@Action}}-mapped method) rejects a disallowed method with the mapped {{bad-request}} result, or with 405 + {{Allow}} when none is mapped, and accepts an allowed one. * *Gap confirmed:* document what is missing (for example, a case the annotations cannot express for Convention actions) and open a New Feature ticket at 8.0.0 for an {{@Action(httpMethod = ...)}} style attribute, linking it here.

title: Struts Boot: run a Struts application from main() with an embedded container and programmatic action registration
Description: h2. Goal Give newcomers a working Struts application with almost no setup: add one dependency, write an action class, run {{main()}}, see the page. No {{web.xml}}, no {{struts.xml}}, no external servlet container. Standalone — no Spring dependency. h2. Minimal scope * New {{struts-boot-starter}} artifact pulling in core and an embedded servlet container (Tomcat), registering {{StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter}} in code. * {{StrutsBoot.run(App.class, args)}} entry point; the application class implements {{StrutsBootApplication}}. * Fluent action registration, fed into the configuration through a single {{ConfigurationProvider}} built on {{PackageConfig}} / {{ActionConfig}} / {{ResultConfig}} builders. No Convention plugin, no classpath scanning. {code:java}public class HelloApp implements StrutsBootApplication { public static void main(String[] args) { StrutsBoot.run(HelloApp.class, args); } @Override public void actions(ActionRegistry actions) { actions.action("hello", HelloAction.class) .success("hello.ftl"); actions.namespace("/admin", admin -> { admin.action("users", UserAction.class) .method("list") .success("admin/users.ftl"); admin.action("users/save", UserAction.class) .method("save") .httpMethods(POST) .result("input", "admin/userForm.ftl") .redirectAction("success", "users"); }); } } {code} * Defaults: each namespace is a package extending {{struts-default}}; top level is namespace {{""}}; {{method}} defaults to {{execute}}; {{success(path)}} is shorthand for {{result("success", path)}}; interceptors default to {{defaultStack}}, overridable per action or namespace by stack name; {{httpMethods(...)}} maps to the http-method restriction from WW-3717. * Views: FreeMarker only, chosen by {{.ftl}} extension, resolved from {{classpath:/templates/}}. * Configuration: the existing {{struts.properties}}; Boot-only settings (port, context path) under a {{struts.boot.*}} prefix. Not {{application.properties}}, to avoid clashing with Spring Boot. * A {{struts.xml}} on the classpath is still loaded alongside the registry. * Runnable fat jar via a Maven plugin. h2. Parked for later * Running an existing Struts WAR as a self-contained jar (migration path). * JSP views in the embedded container. * Gradle plugin. * Alternative containers (Jetty, Undertow). * Fluent definition of custom interceptor stacks. * Global results, global exception mappings, wildcard actions in the registry. * Optional bridge to Convention plugin annotations. * Dev-mode reload of templates and registry. * Project generator / quick-start archetype. * Health and info endpoints.

title: XmlDocConfigurationProvider#verifyAction does not fail startup for a non-public action class
Description: h2. Problem {{XmlDocConfigurationProvider#verifyAction}} is meant to fail fast when an action class declared in XML is not public. It throws a {{ConfigurationException}} with the message "Action class [...] is not public" — but the throw happens inside the same {{try}} block whose {{catch (RuntimeException ex)}} handler logs at INFO ("Unable to verify action class [...] exists at initialization") and carries on. {{ConfigurationException}} extends {{StrutsException}}, which extends {{RuntimeException}}, so the check never takes effect and startup continues. The sibling check works: a class without a public no-arg constructor raises {{NoSuchMethodException}}, which has its own handler that rethrows as {{ConfigurationException}}. h2. Reproduction Calling {{verifyAction}} (with the default {{ObjectFactory}}, so {{isNoArgConstructorRequired()}} is true) on: * a package-private action class → returns normally, nothing but an INFO log line; * a public class without a public no-arg constructor → throws {{ConfigurationException: Action class [...] does not have a public no-arg constructor}}. Confirmed on {{main}} with a throwaway test in {{org.apache.struts2.config.providers}} that injects a {{StrutsXmlConfigurationProvider}} from the test container and calls {{verifyAction}} directly for both classes. h2. Expected A non-public action class fails configuration loading with the "is not public" {{ConfigurationException}}, the same way a missing no-arg constructor does. The {{catch (RuntimeException)}} handler is there for container-specific failures (e.g. request- or session-scoped Spring beans); it should not swallow the provider's own validation errors — for example by rethrowing {{ConfigurationException}} before the generic handler. h2. Notes Found while adding the same check to the Struts Boot registry provider (WW-5791), which fails startup for non-public action classes. There is currently no core test for the non-public branch.

title: Support datetextfield tag in the html5 theme
Description: h2. Problem {{datetextfield}} has a native HTML counterpart, {{input type="date"}}, yet the html5 theme (like the simple theme it extends) renders only a placeholder: "Tag datetextfield works only with the JavaTemplates Plugin!". The only working implementation is in the JavaTemplates plugin's simple theme. h2. Proposal Implement {{template/html5/datetextfield.ftl}} rendering {{input type="date"}}: * The submitted and rendered value uses the ISO {{yyyy-MM-dd}} form that {{input type="date"}} requires, independent of the tag's required {{format}} attribute; define how {{format}} applies in this theme (ignored, or used only for display outside the input) and document it * Common attributes, dynamic attributes and HTML5 constraint attributes ({{min}}, {{max}}, {{required}}) consistent with the other html5 templates * Tests with expected-output fixtures, and the tag reference updated to state html5 support Related: WW-5776 (removal of the tags the html5 theme cannot support)

title: Support java.time types in the datetextfield tag
Description: h2. Problem {{datetextfield}} only works with {{java.util.Date}} properties: * The JavaTemplates {{DateTextFieldHandler}} casts the value straight to {{java.util.Date}}, so a {{LocalDate}} property fails with a {{ClassCastException}} * {{DateTextFieldInterceptor}} reassembles the split fields with {{SimpleDateFormat}} and always sets a {{java.util.Date}} * The html5 template added in WW-5778 renders the ISO {{yyyy-MM-dd}} value from {{java.util.Date}} only {{input type="date"}} maps naturally to {{java.time.LocalDate}}, which is the type most applications now use for a date without a time. h2. Proposal Support {{java.time}} property types (at least {{LocalDate}}) in {{datetextfield}}: * html5 theme: render the ISO {{yyyy-MM-dd}} value for {{LocalDate}} (and define the behaviour for {{LocalDateTime}} / {{ZonedDateTime}} etc. — truncate to the date, or reject) * JavaTemplates theme: format the split fields from {{java.time}} values and have {{DateTextFieldInterceptor}} set the property's declared type * Tests for each supported type, and the tag reference updated to list them Related: WW-5778 (datetextfield in the html5 theme)

title: DateConverter silently drops the time when the date-time separator does not match the locale pattern
Description: When a {{java.util.Date}} (or {{java.sql.Timestamp}}) property receives a date-time whose separator between date and time differs from the locale's date-time pattern, {{DateConverter}} converts it to midnight of that date instead of rejecting it. h2. Example On JDK 25 the {{nl-NL}} SHORT/MEDIUM date-time pattern is {{dd-MM-y, HH:mm:ss}} (JDK 17/21: {{dd-MM-y HH:mm:ss}}, the comma came with newer CLDR data). Submitting {code}24-10-2026 10:15:30 {code} to a {{Date}} property under {{nl-NL}} on JDK 25 yields {{2026-10-24 00:00:00}}. The time is lost without any conversion error. An invalid time is accepted the same way: {{24-10-2026 25:00:00}} also becomes midnight. h2. Cause No date-time format matches the whole input, so the converter falls back to a date-only format ({{dd-MM-y}}). {{SimpleDateFormat.parse(String)}} stops at the end of the date and ignores the trailing text, so the strict re-parse succeeds on the prefix. This exists on {{main}} before WW-5812; WW-5812 only changed which format is selected when one matches the whole input. h2. Possible fix Require the final parse to consume the whole input (a {{ParsePosition}} check, as WW-5812's format selection already does), and throw {{TypeConversionException}} otherwise. This is a behaviour change: any input with trailing text after a valid date, which converts today, would then be rejected. It should be called out in the release notes.

title: DateConverter reads a trailing Z in an ISO date-time as server-local time instead of UTC
Description: {{DateConverter}} accepts ISO date-times such as {{1996-12-19T16:39:57Z}} and {{2026-10-25T05:14:42.000Z}} (the form JavaScript's {{Date.toISOString()}} produces) for {{java.util.Date}} properties, but treats the {{Z}} as a literal. The value is interpreted in the server's default time zone, so a UTC timestamp sent by a client is shifted by the server's offset. Other RFC 3339 forms are not accepted at all: a numeric offset ({{+02:00}}), and fractional seconds with other than three digits. h2. Background Before WW-5813 the converter ignored any text after {{yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss}}, so {{Z}} and {{.SSSZ}} were silently dropped. WW-5813 rejects trailing text, and keeps these two inputs working by adding {{yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'}} and {{yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'}} formats that preserve the previous local-time reading. {{OgnlUtilTest.testSetPropertiesDate}} pins that reading. h2. Fix Reading {{Z}} as UTC changes the instant every existing {{...Z}} value converts to (shifted by the server's offset), silently and without a conversion error, so it goes behind an opt-in flag: * new constant {{struts.converter.date.isoOffsetAware}}, default {{false}} * {{false}}: behaviour as released after WW-5813, {{Z}} read as server-local time * {{true}}: for {{java.util.Date}} (and {{Calendar}}, which goes through it) an ISO date-time with an offset is parsed with {{DateTimeFormatter.ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME}}, so {{Z}} means UTC, numeric offsets are honoured and 0-9 fractional digits are accepted {{java.sql.Timestamp}} (no ISO support today), the {{java.time}} types ({{OffsetDateTime}} already parses offsets) and the JSON plugin's own date handling are out of scope. The default flips to {{true}} in 8.0.0 under a separate ticket.

title: Derive HTML5 min/max and required constraints for temporal controls
Description: h2. Problem HTML5 constraint derivation ({{struts.ui.html5.constraints}}) maps range validators to {{min}}/{{max}} only for {{number}} and {{range}} controls. {{HtmlControlType.supportsRange()}} already includes the temporal controls ({{date}}, {{month}}, {{week}}, {{time}}, {{datetime-local}}), but {{StrutsHtmlConstraintProvider}} deliberately skips them, because their {{min}}/{{max}} values need per-control ISO formatting. As a result, {{DateRangeFieldValidator}} emits nothing. The {{required}} validator has a related gap. {{addRequiredField}} emits {{required}} only for {{radio}} and {{file}}, because other controls submit an empty string, which the {{required}} validator accepts. A temporal control bound to a {{java.util.Date}} (or {{java.time}}) property is different: {{DateConverter}} turns {{""}} into null, so the server rejects the empty value just as the browser would. These controls currently get only {{data-msg-required}}. This affects {{textfield type="date"}} (and the other temporal types) today, and {{datetextfield}} in the html5 theme (WW-5778). h2. Proposal In {{StrutsHtmlConstraintProvider}}, map {{DateRangeFieldValidator}} min/max to {{min}}/{{max}} for temporal controls, formatted per control: * {{date}} → {{yyyy-MM-dd}} * {{month}} → {{yyyy-MM}} * {{week}} → {{YYYY-'W'ww}} (ISO week-based year) * {{time}} → {{HH:mm}} (or {{HH:mm:ss}}) * {{datetime-local}} → {{yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm}} Emit {{required}} from a {{required}} validator on a temporal control only when the bound property's type converts an empty string to null. A {{textfield type="date"}} bound to a {{String}} property must not get it, because the server accepts {{""}} there. The provider currently sees only the control type and the value, so it needs the property type as well. Requirements: * Format the bounds the same way the server compares them, so the browser never rejects a value the server accepts (time zone and truncation for {{java.util.Date}} bounds) * Skip the attribute for controls/value types that cannot be represented exactly, as the numeric path does for fractional {{min}} * Tests for each temporal control, including {{datetextfield}} (replace {{Html5ConstraintRenderingTest.testRendersNoRequiredOnADateTextField}}), and the tag reference updated Related: WW-5778 (datetextfield in the html5 theme), WW-5810 (java.time support in datetextfield)

title: Add a range validator for java.time.LocalDate properties
Description: h2. Problem {{DateRangeFieldValidator}} ({{date}}) is a {{RangeValidatorSupport<Date>}}. On a {{java.time.LocalDate}} property it compares the {{LocalDate}} value against a {{java.util.Date}} bound, which throws {{ClassCastException}}, so a {{LocalDate}} field has no working range validation. {{DateConverter}} and the date tags have supported {{LocalDate}} for some time (WW-5016, WW-5530, WW-5810); the validators have not. h2. Proposal A separate validator, following the one-class-per-type pattern of the existing range validators: * {{LocalDateRangeFieldValidator extends RangeValidatorSupport<LocalDate>}}, registered as {{localdate}} in the default validators * {{min}} / {{max}} as ISO dates ({{2026-01-01}}), plus {{minExpression}} / {{maxExpression}} * annotation {{@LocalDateRangeFieldValidator}}, a {{localDateRangeFields()}} member on {{@Validations}} (with an empty default, so existing code keeps compiling), and processing in {{AnnotationValidationConfigurationBuilder}} * {{LocalDate}} only; {{LocalDateTime}} / {{LocalTime}} can follow on demand {{DateRangeFieldValidator}} stays unchanged. The removed legacy client-side validation never supported {{date}}, so nothing is needed there. Before implementing, check how a string {{min}} / {{max}} param from XML reaches the generic {{setMin(T)}} / {{setMax(T)}} of {{RangeValidatorSupport}}, and that it ends up as a {{LocalDate}}. h2. Requirements * Tests: XML and annotation configuration, inclusive bounds, null value skipped, expressions * Validator reference docs on struts-site Related: WW-5811 (HTML5 {{min}}/{{max}} for {{date}} controls), which will map this validator's bounds directly to {{min="yyyy-MM-dd"}}.

title: Javatemplates plugin renders dynamic attributes differently from the simple theme: values are not HTML-escaped and are evaluated a second time
Description: The javatemplates plugin is documented as a drop-in replacement for the simple theme. {{DynamicAttributesHandler.processDynamicAttributes}} differs from the FreeMarker {{dynamic-attributes.ftl}} in two ways. # Dynamic attribute values are stored with {{Attributes.put}}. Every other handler in the plugin goes through {{Attributes.add}} or {{addIfExists}}, which apply {{escapeHtml4}}, and the FreeMarker template writes the value under the configuration's HTML auto-escaping. {{XHTMLTagSerializer.start}} then writes the stored value between double quotes as it is. # {{UIBean.setDynamicAttributes}} already translates the percent-brace expressions for every component that is not lazily evaluated. The handler tests the resolved value with {{ComponentUtils.isExpression}} again and calls {{findString}} on it, so a value that resolves to text in the percent-brace form is evaluated a second time. The FreeMarker template evaluates only when {{evaluate_dynamic_attributes}} is set, which {{radiomap.ftl}} and {{checkboxlist.ftl}} do because {{Radio}} and {{CheckboxList}} return {{lazyEvaluation() == true}} and render their dynamic attributes per list item. h2. Observed With {{struts.ui.templateSuffix=java}} and the {{hint}} property bound from the request: {code}<s:textfield name="q" data-hint="%{hint}"/> hint = a "b" c java: data-hint="a "b" c" ftl: data-hint="a "b" c" hint = %{1+1} java: data-hint="2" ftl: data-hint="%{1+1}" {code} The standard attributes of the same tag ({{value}}, {{title}}) render identically under both engines. Every tag wired through {{DynamicAttributesHandler}} in {{SimpleTheme}} behaves the same way. h2. Proposed change * Store dynamic attribute values through {{Attributes.add}}, in line with the other handlers and the FreeMarker templates. * Evaluate a dynamic attribute in the handler only when the component is lazily evaluated. {{UIBean}} already knows this through {{lazyEvaluation()}}; expose it as a component parameter so the plugin can read it. {{Radio}} and {{CheckboxList}} keep their per-item evaluation in the handler chain, where {{RadioHandler}} and {{CheckboxListHandler}} push each item before calling {{start}}. h2. Compatibility Under the java engine, a dynamic attribute value is now HTML-escaped once, as it already is under the FreeMarker themes; a value that already contains entities is escaped again, matching the FreeMarker output. A value that resolves to text in the percent-brace form is rendered literally instead of being evaluated, matching the FreeMarker output. Lazily evaluated components are unchanged. h2. Tests * A dynamic attribute whose resolved value contains a double quote renders escaped under the java engine. * A dynamic attribute whose resolved value is in the percent-brace form renders literally on a non-lazy component. * A dynamic attribute on {{Radio}} is still evaluated per item in the handler. * The existing dynamic-attribute rendering tests keep passing for every tag in {{SimpleTheme}}. Reported by Claude and Ada Logics.

title: Radio tag renders its name attribute without HTML escaping, unlike every other form tag
Description: The radio template is the only bundled form template that writes the {{name}} attribute with {{?no_esc}}. Every sibling template (checkbox, checkboxlist, text, select, file, hidden, password, textarea, submit, reset, form) writes it under the FreeMarker auto-escaping configured for the UI templates, and the javatemplates plugin escapes it as well. The exception dates from the original template, which never carried the per-parameter {{?html}} the checkbox template had. When the templates moved to built-in auto-escaping in WW-4972, the radio template kept its previous output by adding {{?no_esc}} to that one attribute. h2. Current behaviour A radio with a name containing a double quote, rendered under the {{simple}}, {{xhtml}} or {{html5}} theme, closes the attribute early: {code}<input type="radio" name="x" onfocus="alert(1)" id="x__onfocus__alert_1_a" value="a"/> {code} A checkboxlist with the same name renders the quote as {{"}}. h2. Expected behaviour The radio name is written the same way as on every other tag, HTML-escaped. h2. Change Remove {{?no_esc}} from the {{name}} attribute in the {{simple}} and {{html5}} radio templates and pin the escaped output with a test. One existing fixture, Radio-6.txt, pins a name containing apostrophes; auto-escaping renders those as {{'}}, as the combobox fixtures already show.

title: StringConverter does not bound integer digits when formatting BigDecimal
Description: WW-5711 bounded {{maximumFractionDigits}} to 340 in {{StringConverter.convertToString()}}, so the length of a formatted {{BigDecimal}} no longer follows a large positive scale. The integer side has no equivalent bound: {{DecimalFormat}} keeps its default {{maximumIntegerDigits}} of {{Integer.MAX_VALUE}}, and for a {{BigDecimal}} with a large negative scale it pads the integer part out to the full value, so the length of the output follows the scale of the value rather than its precision — the counterpart of WW-5711 on the other side of the decimal point. {{setMaximumIntegerDigits}} is not the right bound. {{DecimalFormat}} applies it by dropping the leading digits rather than by rounding, so an ordinary value wider than the bound would format as its trailing digits only. Bound the number of integer digits ({{precision() - scale()}}) to the same 340 instead. A {{BigDecimal}} within that bound formats exactly as before; past it, fall back to {{BigDecimal.toString()}}, which renders the value compactly in scientific notation. Every {{double}} still formats in full — the widest, {{Double.MAX_VALUE}}, has 309 integer digits, and the existing tests pin that. Add a regression test covering the bound on both sides of it.

title: Number tag and localized text arguments do not bound integer digits when formatting BigDecimal
Description: WW-5828 bounded the number of integer digits {{StringConverter}} emits when it formats a {{BigDecimal}}, falling back to {{BigDecimal.toString()}} past the bound so that the length of the output follows the precision of the value rather than its scale. Two other places in core format a {{BigDecimal}} without going through {{StringConverter}}, and neither applies the same bound: * the {{number}} tag formats the value it finds on the stack with {{NumberFormat}} directly; * message arguments passed to {{getText(key, args)}} (also reached from the {{text}} tag with {{param}}, and from validator {{messageParams}}) are formatted by {{MessageFormat}}, which delegates numeric arguments to the locale {{NumberFormat}}. Apply the WW-5828 bound to both paths, sharing the bound rather than duplicating the constant. For message arguments the bound has to be applied through the formatter, not by substituting the argument, since a number-typed message element rejects a {{String}} argument. Values within the bound must render byte-identically to today, including {{currency}} and typed message elements. Same fix on the 6.x line.

title: Upgrade OGNL to version 3.4.17
Description: Bump {{ognl:ognl}} from 3.4.16 to 3.4.17. OGNL 3.4.17 matches property names exactly in {{OgnlRuntime.getReadMethod}} / {{getWriteMethod}}; a mis-cased name no longer resolves to an accessor of a different spelling. One test fixture in {{OgnlSetPossiblePropertyTest}} relied on the case-insensitive lookup and needs updating alongside the bump. Supersedes Dependabot PR [#2103|https://github.com/apache/struts/pull/2103].

title: Exclude java.beans, java.lang.reflect and java.lang.invoke from OGNL member access by default
Description: SecurityMemberAccess checks the declaring class and the target class of every member an OGNL expression resolves against {{struts.excludedClasses}} and {{struts.excludedPackageNames}}. The shipped lists in {{struts-excluded-classes.xml}} name the usual JDK entry points ({{java.lang.Runtime}}, {{java.lang.ProcessBuilder}}, {{java.lang.Class}}, {{java.lang.ClassLoader}}, {{java.io}}, {{java.net}}, {{javax}}, {{sun.reflect}}, ...) but not {{java.beans}}. {{java.beans.Expression}} and {{java.beans.Statement}} perform the method call they describe inside the JDK. An expression that constructs one and calls {{getValue()}} therefore has the inner call made on its behalf, and that call never appears as a member for SecurityMemberAccess to check, so neither the excluded-class check nor the static-method check applies to it. On 7.x the allowlist ({{struts.allowlist.enable=true}} by default) rejects the {{java.beans.Expression}} constructor, so the gap is reachable only where the allowlist has been disabled. On 6.x the allowlist is off by default and the exclusion lists are the only layer. Change, on both lines: * add {{java.beans}}, {{java.lang.reflect}} and {{java.lang.invoke}} to {{struts.excludedPackageNames}} and {{struts.devMode.excludedPackageNames}} in {{struts-excluded-classes.xml}} * a regression test that evaluates such an expression against the shipped configuration with the allowlist disabled {{java.lang.reflect}} and {{java.lang.invoke}} are reachable from an expression today only through a static call or a {{Class}} object, both of which are already rejected; they are added in the same pass for the same reason. The package rule also covers {{java.beans.beancontext}}. An application that needs expression access to a class in one of these packages can re-allow it with {{struts.excludedPackageExemptClasses}}. Reported by Yu Deshui (于得水, @qiushui\_sky) and by Daniel Owens.

title: Action mapping should rely on the servlet path and path info reported by the container
Description: RequestUtils.getServletPath derives the path to map from HttpServletRequest.getRequestURI() in two cases: when the request URI does not end with the servlet path reported by the container (WW-2268, to keep a {{;jsessionid=...}} suffix), and when the container reports an empty servlet path, as it does for a servlet mapped to {{/*}}. In both cases the value comes from the raw request URI, so it differs from the servlet path and path info the container has already decoded: it still carries percent-encoding and path parameters. {{DefaultActionMapper}} then drops everything after the first {{;}}, and {{RestActionMapper}} keeps a trailing {{;edit}} to select the edit method (WW-4585 added the same handling to the {{!method}} form). Every consumer of the helper afterwards works with the container's view of the request (action name and namespace, the exclusion patterns, the static resource lookup, {{<s:include>}} and {{ResourceUtil}}), so the reconstruction is a second interpretation of the same request that can differ from the container's. h2. Proposed change * {{RequestUtils.getServletPath}} returns the servlet path followed by the path info, both as reported by the container; the request URI is no longer consulted. {{getUri}} keeps its include-attribute handling. * {{DefaultActionMapper}} and {{RestActionMapper}} no longer treat {{;}} in the mapped path specially. On a Servlet 3+ container path parameters never reach the servlet path or the path info, so {{;jsessionid=...}} needs no handling in Struts. * The REST plugin's {{;edit}} form ({{GET /movies/Thrillers;edit}}) is removed. {{GET /movies/Thrillers/edit}} is the documented equivalent and continues to work; the plugin documentation drops the {{;edit}} example. * {{ExecuteOperations}} no longer needs its own path-info fallback for an empty servlet path. h2. Compatibility * Applications linking to the REST {{;edit}} form have to switch to {{/edit}}. * With a servlet mapped to {{/*}} in front of Struts, the action path is now taken from the decoded path info rather than from the raw request URI. Same change on the 6.x line. Reported by Svyatoslav Berestovsky.

title: Fetch Metadata policy rejects cross-site POST and HEAD navigations since WW-5753
Description: Follow-up to [WW-5753|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/WW-5753] (PR [#1983|https://github.com/apache/struts/pull/1983]). After WW-5753, {{StrutsResourceIsolationPolicy.isAllowedTopLevelNavigation}} accepts a cross-site request only when {{Sec-Fetch-Mode}} is {{navigate}} *and* the method is {{GET}}. {{FetchMetadataInterceptor}} is part of {{defaultStack}}, so with the default configuration the following now get a 403. Every release since 6.0.0 accepted them: * Cross-site POST navigations, for example a SAML or OIDC {{form_post}} response to an action, or a payment gateway posting the user back to the application. * Cross-site {{HEAD}} navigations. The [Fetch Metadata interceptor documentation|https://struts.apache.org/core-developers/fetch-metadata-interceptor] lists {{HEAD}} alongside {{GET}} as an accepted method. The only way out today is {{exemptedPaths}}. It is matched against {{request.getContextPath()}} ({{FetchMetadataInterceptor}}), so any entry exempts the whole web application, not a single action. h2. Options # Accept a cross-site request when {{Sec-Fetch-Mode}} is {{navigate}}, whatever the method, as long as the destination is not {{object}} or {{embed}}. Cross-site subresource requests stay rejected, and form-post and redirect-back flows keep working. # Keep the GET-only rule, add {{HEAD}}, and document the change as breaking in the 7.5.0 Version Notes and the Migration Guide, with a supported way to exempt individual actions. h2. Also * Decide whether {{exemptedPaths}} should be matched against the request path (servlet path plus path info) rather than the context path. * {{FetchMetadataInterceptorTest.testValidTopLevelNavigation}} sends no {{Sec-Fetch-Site}} header, so it returns at the empty-site check and never reaches the navigation branch. Make it set {{cross-site}}, or drop it in favour of {{testCrossSiteTopLevelGetNavigationAllowed}}. * Add tests for a cross-site POST navigation and a cross-site HEAD navigation, asserting whichever behaviour is chosen.

title: FetchMetadata, COOP and COEP interceptors match exemptedPaths against the context path instead of the request path
Description: Spun off from [WW-5754|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/WW-5754]. {{FetchMetadataInterceptor}}, {{CoopInterceptor}} and {{CoepInterceptor}} all compare each {{exemptedPaths}} entry with the web application's context path: {code:java}String contextPath = request.getContextPath(); if (exemptedPaths.contains(contextPath)) { return invocation.invoke(); } {code} The context path is the same for every request to the application, so since [WW-5083|https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/WW-5083] (6.0.0): * An entry naming an action or URL path, for example {{/saml/acs}}, never matches and silently has no effect. * An entry equal to the context path, for example {{/myapp}}, matches every request and disables the interceptor for the whole application. The tests mask this: {{struts-testing.xml}} configures action-like entries ({{/fetchMetadataExempted}}), and {{FetchMetadataInterceptorTest}} sets {{request.setContextPath("/fetchMetadataExempted")}} to produce a match. All three interceptors are in {{defaultStack}}. Since WW-5753 / WW-5754 the Fetch Metadata policy rejects cross-site POST navigations (SAML/OIDC {{form_post}}, payment-gateway returns), which makes a working per-path exemption more important. h2. Proposed fix * Match entries in all three interceptors against the request path inside the application, {{RequestUtils.getServletPath(request)}} (servlet path plus path info, as used for action mapping since WW-5842). * Use the same value in the log messages, which currently log the context path. * Rewrite the exemption tests to set the servlet path / path info and leave the context path alone; add a case where the context path equals an entry and the request path does not. h2. Compatibility This changes behaviour in both directions and needs a Version Notes / Migration Guide entry: * Applications that listed their context path to disable an interceptor app-wide lose that. The replacement is the interceptor's {{disabled}} parameter, e.g. {{<param name="fetchMetadata.disabled">true</param>}}. * Entries that never matched will start exempting the paths they name. For COOP / COEP that means the headers are no longer sent on those paths. The matching semantics (exact match vs. prefix/wildcard) are documented on the Fetch Metadata, COOP and COEP interceptor pages.

title: doubleselect: preselection in the second list with doubleMultiple has never worked
Description: {{doubleselect.ftl}} in the simple theme preselects the second list's current value inside the generated script. The single-value branch writes {{doubleNameValue}} as a quoted string literal. The branch taken when {{doubleMultiple}} is set writes it unquoted, as the loop bound and in the comparison, so a plain {{String}} becomes a bare identifier and the script fails on page load; a {{Collection}} renders through {{toString}} with the same result, and a {{String[]}} fails the template render. The branch is also chosen by an existence check, so {{doubleMultiple="false"}} takes it too. Present since WW-2809 (2.1.8). {{support/struts-6-x-x}} carries the identical template. The xhtml theme includes the simple template; the html5 theme renders a placeholder for this tag and is unaffected. h2. Proposed change * Normalise {{doubleNameValue}} in {{DoubleListUIBean}} to a list (from a {{String}}, a {{Collection}} or an array) and emit it in the script as an array of quoted, JS-escaped string literals, as the single-value branch already does for one value. * Select the branch on the boolean value of {{doubleMultiple}}, not on its presence. h2. Compatibility Preselecting several values in the second list works. The single-value path renders as before. h2. Tests * A {{String}}, a {{Collection}} and a {{String[]}} under {{doubleMultiple="true"}} each render a quoted list and preselect the matching options. * {{doubleMultiple="false"}} renders the single-value path. * The existing DoubleSelect fixtures keep passing.
